subtopic: RMSNorm vs LayerNorm / Compute and memory pattern
learningObjective: Compare compute and memory patterns of RMSNorm vs LayerNorm and identify which reduction operations each requires.
stem: Compare a per-row RMSNorm — y = x * rsqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) * g — with LayerNorm — y = (x - mean(x)) / sqrt(var(x) + eps) * g + b. Which comparison of reductions and memory is correct?

options.text: Both require exactly one reduction (over the row); RMSNorm reduces sum(x), LayerNorm reduces sum(x^2). Total HBM traffic is identical because both read the row once and write the row once.

LayerNorm requires two reductions over the row (mean and variance) that must be executed in two passes; RMSNorm requires two reductions as well (sum of x and sum of x^2) because rsqrt needs both statistics.

RMSNorm needs one reduction (sum of x^2); LayerNorm can be computed with one reduction (using E[x^2] - E[x]^2) but requires two moments (sum and sum of squares). HBM read of x is once per row in both; RMSNorm skips the mean subtraction and the bias b, giving fewer per-element ops.
RMSNorm requires two passes over x (one to compute mean(x^2), one to normalize); LayerNorm is single-pass because the numerator can subsume the mean in a running formula.

explanation: RMSNorm needs only sum(x^2) to compute rsqrt(mean(x^2) + eps); it does not use the mean of x. LayerNorm needs both mean and variance, but variance can be computed as E[x^2] - E[x]^2, so the two moments can be gathered in a single reduction pass. HBM traffic per row is the same order — one read of x, one write of y — but per-element compute differs: RMSNorm skips the (x - mean) subtraction and does not use bias b. This makes RMSNorm slightly cheaper per element and is why many modern LLMs use it.

optionExplanations.C: Correct: RMSNorm needs one moment (E[x^2]); LayerNorm needs two but can be fused into one pass.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: RMSNorm uses sum(x^2), not sum(x); mixes up the reductions.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: RMSNorm only needs sum(x^2), not both moments; and LayerNorm can be done in one reduction pass.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: both can be done in a single pass with an appropriate algorithm (Welford or two-moment reduction).

assumptions: The full row fits in one program's registers / SMEM for a single-pass implementation; if not, an online algorithm is needed.
eps is a positive scalar to avoid division by zero.
nonImplications: Does not imply RMSNorm is always faster; both are memory-bound and the difference is small in practice.
Does not imply that RMSNorm is a mathematically identical simplification of LayerNorm; they compute different values.

performanceClaim.scope: RMSNorm vs LayerNorm compute and reduction pattern
